About the content

Sources, schedule, badges, and what is still to come

Where the content comes from

The app is built from the course’s own material:

  • the session slides by Qinyun Lin (sessions 1–4, preliminary “v0” versions);
  • the instructor’s Canvas posts for each session: topics, learning objectives and key questions;
  • the course syllabus (learning outcomes, examination) and the literature list;
  • lecture notes taken in class (topics marked ✏️; they also record that the exam tests concepts, not programming).

Explanations, quizzes, drills, simulated figures, R cells, why-questions and written model answers were written for this app. Simulations use made-up data. The course books are cited, not reproduced:

  • Lawson, Banerjee, Haining & Ugarte (eds.) (2016). Handbook of Spatial Epidemiology. CRC Press. Main textbook.
  • Anselin (2024). An Introduction to Spatial Data Science with GeoDa, Volume 1: Exploring Spatial Data. Chapman & Hall/CRC. Chapters 1–7, 10, 13, 16.

Neither book has been used for this version of the app yet.

How the badges were assigned

Badge Rule
🎯 Instructor learning objective The section teaches something stated as a learning objective: in the course syllabus (Session 1: role of place, spatial dependence and heterogeneity, bias from aggregation, measurement and missing data), the Canvas post (Sessions 2 and 4) or the “Learning goals” slide (Session 3)
❓ Instructor’s key question The section answers one of the key questions in the Session 4 Canvas post, or a question the instructor asked on a slide (for example “which is the box map?”, “is π̂ the average of all rates?”, the SAR plausibility and scenario slides)
✏️ Emphasised in class Written down in the lecture notes: spatial file types, DeSO, geocoding, polygon/area, GIS and GeoDa, the social-ecological and life-course models. Where a noted topic also matches an objective (MAUP, the definition), 🎯 is used
📌 Likely exam-relevant (AI-inferred) Inferred from definitions, formulas and worked examples on the slides. Not confirmed
📎 Optional depth Marked “optional depth” on the slide (PC priors), listed as not covered (Session 3 scope slide), or stated as not expected (INLA’s computational details)

Course facts

STA530 Spatial Epidemiology, 3.5 credits, Sahlgrenska Academy, University of Gothenburg. Autumn 2026, 1 October – 3 November, 50% pace, taught in English.

Examination Credits Grades
Individual written exam 2.5 U / G / VG
Active participation in a seminar 1.0 U / G

To pass the course you need G on both; VG on the course needs VG on the written exam.

Software: R (with RStudio or Positron) and GeoDa, to be installed before 13 October.

Notes on the slides

  • Session 3, slide 12 (toy SAR example): the slide shows a direct impact of about 1.019 and indirect impacts of about 0.116. The exact inverse of (I − 0.2W) gives 1.023 and 0.114. The total, 1.25 = β/(1 − ρ), agrees. The app uses the exact values.
  • The slides are preliminary (“v0”) versions. If updated slides are posted, sections may be revised.

Still to come

  • Later sessions, computer labs (GeoDa, R) and the seminar. Labs will be covered as concepts on made-up data, not as solutions.
  • Readings from the two course books, if specific chapters are assigned per session.
  • Any example exam questions from the instructor.

Your progress data

Your review status (Not reviewed / Reviewed / Confident) is stored in this browser’s localStorage under the key sta530_topic_status. It stays between visits on the same browser and device, but not across devices or after clearing site data. Use Export progress on the dashboard to keep a backup.
